passages.t: ‘Sing to Him a new song’: the word that made the world
passages.happening:
Psalm 33 has no heading. It opens with a call to praise. “Rejoice in the LORD, O righteous ones; it is fitting for the upright to praise Him” (verse 1). “Sing to Him a new song; play skillfully with a shout of joy” (verse 3).

The reason is God's word. “By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all the stars by the breath of His mouth” (verse 6). “For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm” (verse 9).

The same God rules over nations. “The LORD frustrates the plans of the nations” (verse 10), but “The counsel of the LORD stands forever” (verse 11). Power does not save anyone: “No king is saved by his vast army” (verse 16). “A horse is a vain hope for salvation” (verse 17).

The psalm ends in quiet trust. “Our soul waits for the LORD; He is our help and our shield” (verse 20). “May Your loving devotion rest on us, O LORD, as we put our hope in You” (verse 22).
passages.hearers:
This is a hymn, a song of praise. Among Psalms 1 to 41, only Psalms 1, 2, 10 and 33 have no heading. Psalm 33 has 22 verses, the same as the number of letters in the Hebrew alphabet, though it is not an alphabet poem.

Verse 2 mentions instruments: the harp and an instrument of ten strings. Israel's worship was loud and skilled.

Verses 6 and 9 echo the first page of the Bible, where God speaks and things come to be. ‘Breath’ in verse 6 is ruach, the word also used for wind and for God's Spirit. Some of Israel's neighbours told of gods fighting the sea (see the note on Psalm 24). Psalm 33 says God only had to speak.

‘Loving devotion’ (hesed) frames the psalm. The earth is full of it (verse 5), and the last verse asks for it to rest on us (verse 22).
passages.later:
Genesis begins with God speaking: “And God said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light” (Genesis 1:3). John's Gospel says of the Word who became flesh, “Through Him all things were made” (John 1:3). Hebrews says, “the universe was formed at God's command” (Hebrews 11:3).

The ‘new song’ of verse 3 is sung in heaven in Revelation, to the Lamb: “Worthy are You to take the scroll and open its seals” (Revelation 5:9).
passages.asks:
The psalm asks what you hope in. Verses 16 and 17 list the things people trust: armies, strength, horses. Ours might be savings, health or a plan. None of them is evil. None of them saves.

It also asks you to sing. A ‘new song’ does not have to be a new tune. It is praise that comes fresh, because you have seen God at work again.
